issues.legal_issue: A claim seeking relief from a receiver’s act of taking or attaching property in which the insolvent allegedly had no interest must be brought under the provision governing applications against a receiver, rather than treated as an application under the provision defining the insolvency court’s jurisdiction.
material_facts: A receiver in insolvency took possession of and attached property that a third party claimed belonged exclusively to him and was not liable to be taken for the insolvent’s estate.
The third party sought release of the property and restoration of possession, filing his objection after the receiver’s act and beyond the period allowed for applications against a receiver.
The specific taking and attachment complained of were not acts carried out under an express court direction concerning that property.
issues.conclusion: The objection was an application under section 68 of the Provincial Insolvency Act and was barred because it was filed after the prescribed 21-day period. Section 4 did not provide an alternative application route to avoid that limit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4(1) and (2) defines the insolvency court’s jurisdiction to decide questions arising in insolvency, including questions of title, but does not prescribe a procedure for seeking relief. Section 68 provides the procedure for a person aggrieved by a receiver’s act or decision to apply to the court and requires the application to be made within 21 days. Because section 4 is expressly subject to the Act, it cannot be used to avoid section 68’s time limit. A person aggrieved by a receiver’s act may instead pursue relief under ordinary law. An application complaining of an act done by the receiver under an express court direction is different, because the act is ministerial and the complaint is not against the receiver’s own act. The Court approved Daulat Ram v. Bansilal, AIR 1937 Lahore 2, and disapproved Venkatarama v. Angathayammal, AIR 1933 Madras 471, and Heerabai v. Official Receiver, AIR 1963 AP 296; it distinguished Nathu Ram v. Madan Gopal, AIR 1932 Allahabad 408, where the attachment was made under a court order.

rule.if: insolvency_receiver_review and third_party_claims_property_not_belonging_to_insolvent and receiver_act_not_expressly_court_directed and application_filed_after_allowed_period

predicates.insolvency_receiver_review: The proceeding seeks review or relief in an insolvency matter concerning an act of the receiver.
predicates.third_party_claims_property_not_belongin: A person other than the insolvent claims that property taken or attached by the receiver does not belong to the insolvent’s estate.
predicates.receiver_act_not_expressly_court_directe: The receiver took or attached the disputed property without an express court direction to do that specific act.
predicates.application_filed_after_allowed_period: The person sought review after the period allowed for an application challenging the receiver’s act had expired.

issues.definition: When a third party seeks relief in an insolvency proceeding from a receiver’s non-court-directed act against property claimed not to belong to the insolvent, filing after the allowed period makes the application untimely.
